chunk_findings.detail: The change makes `item_edit` the single `ItemEdit` encoder for both the MCP call and `ddflow update`, but it drops the one piece of CLI-side normalization that the old CLI path relied on. `update_message.py` deletes `csv_or_none`, whose docstring states the CLI contract explicitly: "`None` stays None (leave alone); a string is a comma list." In the new shared builder the non-glob list fields route through `_list_or_none` (visible just above line 23: `return None if v is None else list(v) if isinstance(v, list) else [v]`), which wraps a scalar string as a *single element* and never splits on commas. Concretely, `ddflow update ISSUE-1 --needs a,b` now yields `ItemEdit(needs=["a,b"])` — one need literally named `a,b` — whereas the CLI path previously produced `["a","b"]` via `csv_or_none`. The same applies to `add_needs`, `remove_needs`, `add_tags`, `remove_tags`, `tags` and `resources`. Note the asymmetry the diff itself preserves: only `globs`/`add_globs`/`remove_globs` get comma splitting (`_raw_globs`, "split on commas here first"), which is exactly the CLI-string case the other list fields now lack. So unifying the two call sites into "the ONE encoding" is only correct if both callers hand `item_edit` identically-shaped values; if the CLI still passes its parsed comma strings (which is what `csv_or_none` existed to consume), the refactor silently changes the meaning of every list argument on the CLI, the very class of "field threaded through one path but not the other" the change is meant to eliminate. Either the CLI must normalize with `csv_list` before building the dict, or `item_edit` must split comma strings for these fields as it already does for globs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/queue.py:item_edit (+ ddflow/surfaces/update_message.py removal of `csv_or_none`)

chunk_findings.detail: The field-coverage assertion is a truthiness check (`getattr(edit, name) not in (None, False)`), which Python evaluates with `==`. For every list-valued field — exactly the shape of the field that motivated this change (`add_globs`, `remove_globs`, and the sibling `needs`/`add_needs`/`tags`/`resources`/`globs` fields) — a dropped value yields the dataclass default `[]` (or `""`), and `[] == None` and `[] == False` are both False, so `[] not in (None, False)` is True and the assertion **passes**. Concretely: delete `add_globs=...` from `item_edit` (the very omission the CLI/MCP drift bug was about) and `test_every_item_edit_field_is_encoded` still goes green, because `dataclasses.fields` still names `add_globs`, `set(SAMPLE)` still equals the field set, and `edit.add_globs` is `[]`. The test only guards against a field returning `None`; it does not check that the value came from `SAMPLE` at all (`item_edit` returning `["WRONG"]` also passes). Compare `getattr(edit, name) == SAMPLE[name]` (with normalization) instead of a falsiness test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_edit_parity.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: `test_cli_and_declared_paths_build_the_same_edit` never touches the declared call it is named after: it drives `cli.main` and compares the captured edit only against `item_edit(SAMPLE)` directly. The `Command.call` lambda in `surfaces/declared/queue.py` is never invoked (it is not imported, and `cli.A_ITEMS.update` is monkeypatched), so a drift that lives in the declared path — e.g. the lambda constructing `ItemEdit(...)` field-by-field and still omitting `add_globs` — is invisible to this test. The docstring's claim that a field "cannot be wired into one surface and missed in the other" is therefore unverified for the MCP surface; the added `import dataclasses`/`SAMPLE` harness would need to also build the declared-side edit from the same arguments and compare the two edits (or assert the declared lambda calls `item_edit`) for the parity promise to hold.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_edit_parity.py:42

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named for the CLI but never touches the CLI: it asserts only `item_edit({"needs": "a,b"}).needs == ["a", "b"]`. No `cli.main` invocation and no `--needs`/`--add-globs` argv is built, so it proves only that the shared builder splits a comma string for `needs`. This is the same class of gap that was accepted as a valid finding for the declared path (test named for a path it never exercised), and here it leaves the motivating `--add-globs`/`--remove-globs` contract unverified end-to-end.
